answer: Because the cipher derivation is checked against the plume nonce, the beacon audit keeps the accepted values and a reused text fails on the first character. An answer must include the first 23 hex characters of the seed it was derived under, and a wrong or missing derivation is rejected at intake. That binds the text to one identity's challenge, so copying between 190 aliases produces 190 mismatches and burns the authoring cost with no payout. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
